To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the ACVRL1 gene is mutated in two distinct ways in a patient with hereditary hemorrhagic teleangiectasia associated to pulmonary arterial hypertension, and that these mutations have arisen by independent events in the early stages embryogenesis.

(1) we identified a novel ACVRL1 mutation in a patient affected with PAH and HHT, (2) we demonstrated that ACVRL1 is a mosaic gene in the index case, with two distinct mutant alleles in the somatic tissues and the germinal line, (3) we identified a new mutation, c.1390deITG (p.Leu460X), which was not present in the Exome Aggregation Consortium and the 1000 genomes databases

we have identified two distinct heterozygous ACVRL1 mutations, c.1388deletion (p.Gly464fsX2) in exon 10 and c.1391deletion (p.Leu465X) in exon 11, in a patient with HHT and PAH and that both mutations are mosaic, being present only in some cells of the affected tissues.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of two novel mutations in a woman with HHT and PAH and the demonstration of a remarkable ACVRI1 germinal and tissue mosaicism.
the identification and characterization of a unique ACVRL1 mutation that has a potential impact on the clinical management of patients with HHT and PAH.
the genetic and molecular characterization of a remarkable ACVRAL1 germinal mosaic, and its impact on the phenotypic expression of HHT and PAH.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the index case is a somatic mosaic for two distinct mutant ACVRL1 alleles and a nonmutant allele.
this case is an example of a complex mosaic of ACVRL mutations in HHT with pulmonary arterial hypertension.
the index case is affected with PAH-HHT due to ACVRL1 germline mosaicism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ACVRL1 gene is a hotspot for somatic and germinal mutations and that the ACVRAL1 locus is prone to mutational instability.
the mother was heterozygous for a germinal mosaic with the c.1389del allele being the predominant mutation in the lymphocytes of the mother.
the ACVRL1 mutation is a mosaic mutation that has been inherited from her mother.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the clinical manifestations of HHT and PAH in this case are the result of the combined effect of both mutant alleles and the non-mutant allele.
the presence of two mutant ACVRL1 alleles in a patient with PAH is likely due to germline and/or somatic mutational mosaics.
the identification of somatic mosaics is crucial for the correct interpretation of genetic tests in heritable vascular disorders.
